resources.title: Lelañea — where to turn in a crisis

provenance.note: Drafted for the crisis path of §12 (f-safety t-58). These are the words a person reads at the worst moment they will ever bring to the app, and the services are named, so both the copy and every number wait on her sign-off — and on a check that each service is still answering at the number given — before this reaches anyone outside development.

notes: Never a model's words: this file is shown as it is, by code, whether or not any model is reachable.
A region is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code read from the person's language preference (en-GB → GB). No region, or one not listed here, gets the international entry and the local emergency line.
Keep each service to what a person can act on immediately: who, how to reach them, and when.

copy.hardIntro: It sounds like you might be in real danger right now. You deserve support from a person, straight away — this app can't give you that, but these people can.
copy.softIntro: If things feel like too much right now, you don't have to carry it alone. These people are there to talk, any time.
copy.emergency: If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number now.
copy.keptMessage: What you wrote is still in the box — nothing has been sent or lost.

international.name: Find A Helpline
international.hours: A free directory of crisis lines in over 130 countries
